chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr, from his father, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:
Regarding a eunuch who deceived a Muslim woman about himself, and so married her,
He said: “They are to be separated if the woman wishes, and his head is to be struck. But if she accepts and remains with him, then after having accepted, she no longer has the right to refuse him.”

key_terms.تَأْبَاهُ: to refuse him or reject him
key_terms.خَصِيٍّ: a eunuch; a man whose condition is legally relevant to the marriage case discussed
key_terms.دَلَّسَ: deceived or concealed a defect fraudulently
key_terms.رَضِيَتْ: she accepted or consented after knowing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man deceives a woman about a condition affecting marriage before marrying her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who concealed a physical condition from a Muslim woman before marriage. The woman is given the option to separate, and the man is subject to punishment for deception; however, if she knowingly accepts the situation and remains with him, she cannot later revoke the marriage on that basis.
